threads_text: NVIDIA is putting $3 billion into Meta's stock offering and teaming up on Meta's Muse AI agent, while Meta buys more Vera Rubin chips. The chip seller is now also a shareholder in one of its biggest buyers. Is this smart business or AI money going in circles?
caption:
NVIDIA says it will invest $3 billion in Meta's stock offering as the two expand their work on Meta's Muse assistant and Muse models.
Meta plans to add more NVIDIA Vera Rubin systems, Vera CPUs, Spectrum-X networking and BlueField-4.
Meta also upsized its common stock sale to $25 billion, priced at $625 a share.

Is NVIDIA buying into its own customer a smart bet or a red flag?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

site_article.headline: NVIDIA to invest $3 billion in Meta as the companies expand work on Muse
site_article.dek: The chipmaker will buy into Meta's stock offering while Meta adds more NVIDIA hardware to run its Muse agent and models.
site_article.summary: NVIDIA said on October 27, 2026 that it will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering as part of a broader partnership on Meta's Muse assistant and Muse family of models. Meta plans to expand its use of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin systems, Vera CPUs and networking gear.
site_article.seo_title: NVIDIA to invest $3 billion in Meta, expand Muse AI partnership
site_article.seo_description: NVIDIA will put $3 billion into Meta's stock offering and work with Meta on its Muse AI agent and models, while Meta adds Vera Rubin hardware.
site_article.answer_summary: NVIDIA is investing $3 billion in Meta's equity offering and expanding its technical partnership with Meta on the Muse assistant and Muse models, with Meta committing to deploy more NVIDIA data center hardware.
site_article.hero_alt: A forklift lifts an oversized AI chip with the NVIDIA logo toward a loading bay marked with the Meta logo.

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA said on October 27, 2026 that it will invest $3 billion in Meta Platforms' equity offering, as part of an expanded partnership centered on Meta's Muse assistant and the Muse family of AI models, according to a company announcement and a Reuters report.

The announcement describes the investment as proposed. Forward looking statements in the release say its completion depends on customary closing conditions, and neither company disclosed how many shares NVIDIA will receive or what stake the purchase represents.

The companies said they will work together to improve inference and training performance for Muse and the wider Muse model family. NVIDIA said the joint work is meant to optimize workflows, raise performance and lower total cost of ownership, and it tied the effort to demand for useful AI agents.

NVIDIA and Meta also said they will consider further collaboration on the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture. In the announcement, OpenShell is described as supporting safe deployment of agents, while NVIDIA Sentry is presented as a tool for monitoring agent behavior.

On the hardware side, Meta plans to expand its deployment of NVIDIA infrastructure, including Vera Rubin systems and Vera CPUs, to power next generation AI agents. Meta will also deploy NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4 to improve efficiency and throughput in its data centers.

NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang said the companies are expanding their partnership "to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end" for AI agents. Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg said, "Muse is how we bring personal superintelligence to everyone."

Meta launched Muse, a personal AI agent powered by its Muse Spark model, on September 8, 2026, and followed with the Muse Wonder models on October 12 and the downloadable Muse Spark Open model on October 15, according to Blockchain.News. Investing.com reported that the Muse app became one of the most downloaded apps within a week of its launch.

The NVIDIA investment lands in the middle of a large capital raise by Meta. According to Investing.com, Meta upsized its common stock offering to $25 billion from $22.5 billion, and together with a depositary share offering the sale could raise up to $37.5 billion. The common stock was priced at $625 a share and the depositary shares at $50 each.
Meta has said the money is mainly meant to fund its AI infrastructure buildout, and it has outlined a separate plan to sell $60 billion of non voting shares in 2027, Investing.com reported.

The deal extends a relationship the two companies formalized earlier in the year. In February 2026, Meta announced a multi year strategic partnership with NVIDIA covering large scale deployment for AI training and inference, and adopted NVIDIA Confidential Computing for WhatsApp private messaging along with Spectrum-X Ethernet across its infrastructure, Unite.AI reported.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the arrangement ties NVIDIA more closely to one of its largest customers on both sides of the ledger: NVIDIA becomes a shareholder in Meta while Meta commits to buying more of NVIDIA's newest systems. The companies have not published performance numbers for Muse on the new hardware, so the technical gains remain a stated goal rather than a measured result.
The next markers to watch are the closing of NVIDIA's $3 billion purchase and any figures Meta shares on how Muse performs and grows once more Vera Rubin capacity comes online.
